the BBC–ITVs 2005 exit poll was a good one, and the methodology used to conduct and analyse it was sound.
the exit poll data were collected with a coverage of around 90% of the vote and with a mean absolute error of around 1.5 percentage points.
the exit poll data were of high quality, that the statistical modelling of those data was of high quality and that the exit poll forecasts were of high quality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis issues that arise in the context of an exit poll for a national election in which the outcome is decided by a single member plurality voting system.
the development of methods for exit polls in a cold climate.
the design of the exit poll, its coverage and its accuracy.

, despite the many problems, the 2005 exit poll was a success, and the lessons learnt from it will be of use in future exit polling in Britain.
